s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the vector and pathogen of malaria?
x: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito and is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan.
tq: Match the disease with its characteristic vector and pathogen.

s: Which of the following species of Plasmodium is described as the deadliest form of malaria?
x: Plasmodium falciparum is identified as the deadliest among the listed malaria-causing species.
tq: Use the species-specific distinction rather than the general disease name.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Malaria destroys red blood cells.
2. Dengue mainly affects platelets.
3. Chikungunya is caused by an alphavirus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Malaria destroys red blood cells, dengue mainly affects platelets, and chikungunya is caused by an alphavirus. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
tq: Check each disease against its distinctive pathological or virological feature.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Zika is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Japanese encephalitis is associated with Culex, yellow fever with Aedes or Haemagogus, and sleeping sickness with the tsetse fly.
tq: Eliminate options by identifying the specific vector associated with each disease.

s: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes and is amplified by pigs?
x: Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, and pigs act as amplifying hosts.
tq: Combine the vector clue with the amplifying-host clue.

s: With reference to kala-azar, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It is spread by Aedes and is caused by a flavivirus.
It is spread by a tsetse fly and is caused by Trypanosoma brucei.
It is spread by a sandfly and is caused by Leishmania donovani.
It is spread by Culex and is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti.
x: Kala-azar, or visceral leishmaniasis, is transmitted by the sandfly, not by a mosquito, and is caused by Leishmania donovani.
tq: Distinguish the sandfly-transmitted disease from mosquito-borne diseases.

s: Which one of the following diseases is NOT spread by a mosquito?
x: Scrub typhus is transmitted by the chigger mite. Lymphatic filariasis, Japanese encephalitis and dengue are mosquito-borne diseases.
tq: Find the non-mosquito vector among otherwise mosquito-associated diseases.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Disease)
 a. Lymphatic filariasis
 b. Sleeping sickness
 c. Scrub typhus
 d. Plague
List-II (Vector)
 i. Rat flea
 ii. Tsetse fly
 iii. Culex quinquefasciatus
 iv. Chigger mite
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Lymphatic filariasis is transmitted by Culex quinquefasciatus, sleeping sickness by the tsetse fly, scrub typhus by the chigger mite, and plague by the rat flea.
tq: Start from the sure vector-disease pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Lymphatic filariasis is caused by the nematode Wuchereria bancrofti. Orientia tsutsugamushi causes scrub typhus, Trypanosoma brucei causes sleeping sickness, and Yersinia pestis causes plague.
tq: Use pathogen names to separate diseases with similar vector-borne transmission.

s:
Consider the following statements about Wolbachia:
1. It is a natural intracellular Gram-negative bacterium found in 40–60% of insect species.
2. It is harmful to humans.
3. It is not native to Aedes aegypti or Anopheles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Wolbachia is found naturally in 40–60% of insect species and is harmless to humans. It is not native to Aedes aegypti or Anopheles.
tq: Reject the absolute health claim and retain the two specific biological characteristics.

s: Wolbachia can suppress mosquito-borne pathogen transmission mainly through which combination of mechanisms?
x: Wolbachia acts through cytoplasmic incompatibility, in which mismatched eggs fail to hatch, and through pathogen blocking. The method does not require genetic modification or pesticides.
tq: Identify the biological mechanism rather than an unrelated mosquito-control method.

s: The Verily ‘Debug’ project of 2026 involved the release of which of the following?
x: The project involved releasing Wolbachia-carrying, non-biting male Culex quinquefasciatus, a vector associated with West Nile and St Louis encephalitis.
tq: Use the project-specific organism and sex as the decisive clues.

s: Which of the following diseases are covered under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme as listed?
o: Dengue, hepatitis A, typhoid, chikungunya, malaria and plague
Malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis
Japanese encephalitis, measles, malaria, influenza, kala-azar and cholera
Malaria, tuberculosis, dengue, cholera, kala-azar and rabies
x: The six listed diseases are malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis.
tq: Recall the complete programme coverage list without adding unrelated diseases.

s: Which two diseases under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme are described as outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive?
x: Malaria and dengue are identified as outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive diseases under the programme.
tq: Focus on the stated comparison within the programme list.

s: The Widal test is associated with the diagnosis of which disease?
x: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, and the Widal test is associated with its diagnosis.
tq: Link the named diagnostic test to its specific water-borne disease.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae. Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, while acute diarrhoea and dysentery may involve Shigella, E. coli and rotavirus.
tq: Separate the principal pathogen from pathogens of other faecal-oral diseases.

s: The severe dehydration associated with cholera is primarily caused by which of the following?
o: A deficiency of fluoride in drinking water
Destruction of red blood cells by Plasmodium
A toxin produced by Vibrio cholerae
x: Cholera produces severe dehydration through the toxin of Vibrio cholerae; oral rehydration solution is used to replace lost fluids and electrolytes.
tq: Connect the disease complication with its stated causal mechanism and remedy.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis A and E can spread through the faecal-oral route.
2. Hepatitis B and C are generally blood-borne rather than water-borne.
3. Tuberculosis is an airborne disease, not a water-borne disease.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Hepatitis A and E are faecal-oral diseases, hepatitis B and C are blood-borne, and tuberculosis is airborne rather than water-borne.
tq: Use the transmission-route contrast to identify all correct statements.

s: Which one of the following is the correct set of diseases commonly spread through the faecal-oral route by contaminated water or food?
o: Tuberculosis, hepatitis B, malaria, dengue and rabies
Japanese encephalitis, cholera, hepatitis B, scrub typhus and influenza
Cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio
Hepatitis C, sleeping sickness, yellow fever, typhoid and plague
x: The faecal-oral group includes cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio.
tq: Identify the complete transmission-route group and reject airborne, blood-borne and vector-borne diseases.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Nitrate contamination is associated with blue-baby syndrome. Fluorosis is associated with fluoride contamination.
tq: Find the swapped chemical-contamination pair.

s: Fluoride contamination of drinking water is associated with which condition?
x: Excess fluoride in drinking water causes fluorosis. Minamata disease is linked to mercury, blue-baby syndrome to nitrate and itai-itai disease to cadmium.
tq: Use the pollutant-condition association rather than the disease name alone.

s: Approximately how many children die daily worldwide from preventable water- and sanitation-related diseases?
x: The stated estimate is approximately 5,000 children every day worldwide.
tq: Distinguish the order of magnitude in the quantitative estimate.

s: Which one of the following sets contains diseases whose spread can be associated with floods?
o: Scrub typhus, polio, cancer and asthma
Hepatitis B, AIDS, dengue and influenza
x: Floods can spread cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and leptospirosis, in addition to supporting the spread of some vector-borne diseases.
tq: Recognise the environmental-disaster cluster of water-related diseases.

s: According to the cited Andhra Pradesh assessment for 2025–26, water-borne outbreaks declined by approximately:
x: The reported decline in water-borne outbreaks was 62.7%. The other figures refer to food-borne outbreaks, all outbreaks or diarrhoea deaths.
tq: Separate closely related percentages by the indicator to which each belongs.

s: Which one of the following correctly presents the cited Andhra Pradesh changes?
o: Diarrhoea deaths down 72% and food-borne outbreaks down 21%
Diarrhoea deaths down 21% and food-borne outbreaks down 72%
ADD cases down 47% and all outbreaks down 9.63%
All outbreaks down 62.7% and water-borne outbreaks down 9.63%
x: The cited figures are a 72% decline in diarrhoea deaths and a 21% decline in food-borne outbreaks. All outbreaks declined by 47%, while ADD cases declined by 9.63%.
tq: Match each percentage with the correct indicator instead of treating the figures as interchangeable.

s: Which of the following is a set of measures identified for addressing water and sanitation-related disease risks?
o: Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT
National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, BCG and ORS
AMRUT, Widal test and Wolbachia release
Swachh Bharat Mission, Widal test and DPT
x: Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT are identified as relevant remedies or interventions.
tq: Distinguish programmes and remedies from diagnostic tests, vaccines and vector-control methods.

s: The organ system primarily affected by air pollution is the:
x: Air pollution primarily affects the respiratory system, although it is also associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke and lung cancer.
tq: Select the principal health system rather than a secondary effect.

s:
Consider the following statements about the health effects of air pollution:
1. It can contribute to heart disease and stroke.
2. It is associated with lung cancer.
3. Pollens, spores, bacteria and viruses can act as triggers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Air pollution has respiratory and cardiovascular effects, is associated with lung cancer, and may involve biological triggers such as pollens, spores, bacteria and viruses.
tq: Treat the respiratory, cardiovascular and biological-trigger effects as separate propositions.

s:
Noise pollution is associated with which of the following health effects?
1. Hearing loss
2. Hypertension
3. Sleep disorders
4. Anxiety
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Noise pollution is associated with hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety.
tq: Check whether all listed effects belong to the same environmental-health category.

s: According to the World Health Organization figure cited for 2019, ambient outdoor air pollution caused approximately how many premature deaths?
x: The cited WHO estimate is 4.2 million premature deaths from ambient outdoor air pollution in 2019.
tq: Use the scale of the statistic to distinguish millions from thousands and crores.

s: A public-health assessment is examining premature mortality and time lived with disability together. Which measure is most appropriate for this purpose?
x: DALY combines years of life lost due to premature death and years lived with disability, making it a disease-burden metric.
tq: Identify the metric from the components described in the scenario.

s: Which of the following diseases is NOT included among the diseases covered under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP), now known as NCVBDC?
x: NCVBDC covers malaria, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis. Tuberculosis is not a vector-borne disease covered under this programme.
tq: Find the disease belonging to a neighbouring health programme rather than the listed vector-borne group.
sec: Vector control and elimination - NFME, MERA, Wolbachia, Gambusia, Bti

s:
Which of the following diseases have been specifically targeted for elimination under India’s vector-control programme?
1. Malaria
2. Lymphatic filariasis
3. Kala-azar
4. Dengue
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar are targeted for elimination. Dengue is outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive, but it is not listed here as an elimination target.
tq: Separate elimination targets from diseases managed mainly through outbreak control.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding vector-borne diseases:
1. Malaria and dengue are outbreak-prone diseases.
2. Malaria and dengue are climate-sensitive diseases.
3. Source reduction is one of the tools of vector control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Malaria and dengue are both outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive. Source reduction, along with IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish and bio-larvicides, is a recognised vector-control tool.
tq: Use the inclusive option when all the carefully worded functional statements are supported.

s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016–2030) aims to achieve which of the following?

s: MERA India is associated with which of the following?
o: National Dengue Eradication and Research Authority
Malaria Emergency Response Administration of WHO

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

A. Gambusia
B. Bti
C. Wolbachia
D. Guppy

List-II (Description)

Codes:
A B C D
(a) 2 1 3 2
(b) 1 2 3 1
(c) 2 3 1 2
(d) 3 1 2 3

s:
With reference to Wolbachia, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Gram-negative bacterium found naturally in 40–60% of insects.
2. It is naturally present in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.
3. It can cause cytoplasmic incompatibility in which eggs fail to develop.
4. It can contribute to pathogen blocking.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Wolbachia is a Gram-negative bacterium found in 40–60% of insects. It causes cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking, but it is naturally absent in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.
tq: The false statement reverses the important absence of Wolbachia in the named mosquito genera.

s: In the Verily ‘Debug’ approach described for vector suppression, Wolbachia-carrying males were used to suppress which mosquito species?
x: The Verily ‘Debug’ approach used Wolbachia-carrying males to suppress Culex quinquefasciatus, a vector associated with West Nile and St Louis encephalitis.
tq: Discriminate between closely related mosquito genera by linking the intervention to the exact species.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Verily ‘Debug’ method mentioned in relation to mosquito control?
o: Introduction of Gambusia into urban drinking-water tanks
Spraying of Bti over all adult mosquito habitats
Release of Wolbachia-carrying males without using genetic modification or pesticides
Release of genetically modified females with pesticide-resistant genes
x: The method involved Wolbachia-carrying males and did not use genetic modification or pesticides.
tq: Identify the method by separating biological suppression from genetic modification and chemical control.

s: Which of the following pairs of countries was certified malaria-free by WHO in South Asia in 2015 and 2016, respectively?

tq: Use the year sequence to distinguish two closely associated regional certifications.

s:
Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause or facilitating factor of antimicrobial resistance?
1. Overuse or misuse of antibiotics
2. Self-medication
3. Poor sanitation
4. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Overuse or misuse, self-medication and poor sanitation contribute to AMR. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use is not a cause; unregulated veterinary drug use is a concern.
tq: Find the carefully reversed statement in an otherwise familiar list of AMR causes.

s:
Antimicrobial resistance is regarded as a One Health problem primarily because it is influenced by antibiotic use and waste practices in which of the following settings?
1. Humans
2. Livestock and farms
3. Veterinary practice
4. Pharmaceutical effluent and waste systems
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: AMR is driven by interconnected human, animal, agricultural, veterinary and environmental factors, including pharmaceutical effluents and poor waste control.
tq: Recognise the One Health pattern when human, animal and environmental domains are combined.
sec: Antimicrobial resistance - causes, biofilms, antibiotics, NAP-AMR, Red Line

s: What are biofilms in the context of antimicrobial resistance?
o: Microbial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix
Synthetic capsules used to deliver antibiotics
Dead bacterial cells produced after antibiotic treatment
Free-floating viruses that destroy antibiotic molecules
x: Biofilms are microbial or bacterial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix, which shields them from antibiotics and, in many cases, from host immunity.
tq: Use the exact structural definition rather than a broad association with infection.

s: The principal protective significance of a bacterial biofilm is that it:
o: increases the oxygen content of infected tissue
shields bacteria from antibiotics and immunity
x: The slimy matrix of a biofilm protects bacterial communities from antibiotics and host immunity, making infections difficult to treat.
tq: Translate the definition of a biofilm into its clinical consequence.
sec: Antimicrobial resistance - causes, biofilms, antibiotics, NAP-AMR, Red Line

s: Nafithromycin, marketed as ‘Miqnaf’, is correctly described as which of the following?
o: India’s first indigenous antiviral for dengue
A fungal vaccine developed for tuberculosis
A carbapenem developed exclusively for hospital-acquired malaria
India’s first indigenous macrolide for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia
x: Nafithromycin, or Miqnaf, is India’s first indigenous macrolide antibiotic intended for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
tq: Link the drug name with its exact class, origin and therapeutic indication.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nafithromycin:

2. It was launched by Dr Jitendra Singh.
3. It was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support.

x: Nafithromycin was launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh and was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support. It was not developed by Sun Pharma.

A red vertical line on packs of prescription-only antibiotics
A red band on all vaccines supplied under UIP
A red symbol on blood bags meant for transfusion

Monitoring only antimicrobial resistance in hospitals
Recording only adult BCG doses in Andhra Pradesh

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Climate change can intensify heatwaves, floods and cyclones.
2. Malaria, dengue and Japanese encephalitis are among the vector-borne diseases affected by climate change.
3. About 3.6 billion people live in highly climate-vulnerable areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Climate change increases the risk of extreme weather events and several vector-borne diseases, and about 3.6 billion people are reported to live in highly vulnerable areas.
tq: Check whether all three linked statements describe the same climate-health relationship.

s: According to the Dasra report ‘Under the Weather’, approximately what proportion of Indian districts are at high risk from extreme weather?
x: The Dasra report ‘Under the Weather’ estimated that approximately 40% of Indian districts are at high risk from extreme weather.
tq: Distinguish the reported percentage from nearby rounded alternatives.

s: The World Health Organization has estimated that climate change may cause approximately how many additional deaths annually during 2030–2050 from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea and heat?
x: The estimate is approximately 2.5 lakh additional deaths annually during 2030–2050 from the specified climate-sensitive causes.
tq: Split the numerical options by magnitude before selecting the reported estimate.

s: Which one of the following diseases primarily affects platelets?
x: Dengue is associated with a fall in platelet count. Filariasis affects the lymphatic system, amoebiasis the large intestine and ascariasis the small intestine.
tq: Use the disease-to-blood-component association rather than the organ associations.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Malaria parasites first multiply in the liver and subsequently infect which blood component?
x: Malaria parasites first undergo development in the liver and then infect red blood cells.
tq: Follow the biological sequence from the initial organ to the blood component.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Filariasis affects the lymphatic system and may cause elephantiasis. Tuberculosis affects the lungs, amoebiasis the large intestine and ascariasis the small intestine.
tq: Find the one correct disease-organ pair among swapped organ distractors.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Amoebiasis is primarily an infection of the:
o: Lymphatic system caused by filarial worms
Small intestine caused by Ascaris lumbricoides
Large intestine caused by Entamoeba histolytica
x: Amoebiasis affects the large intestine and is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
tq: Discriminate between similar disease-organ and causative-organism combinations.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Malaria — liver followed by red blood cells
x: Dengue is associated with platelets. The lymphatic system and elephantiasis are associated with filariasis.
tq: Find the deliberately swapped disease-organ association.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Which species of Plasmodium is most lethal and is particularly associated with cerebral malaria?
x: Plasmodium falciparum is the most lethal human-infecting malaria parasite and may cause cerebral malaria.
tq: Identify the species linked with the severe clinical form.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s:
Consider the following species:
1. Plasmodium falciparum
2. Plasmodium vivax
3. Plasmodium malariae
4. Plasmodium ovale
5. Plasmodium knowlesi
Which of the above infect humans?
x: All five listed species—P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale and P. knowlesi—are recognised as infecting humans.
tq: Check the complete species list rather than stopping at the commonly known species.
sec: Disease → organ or blood component; Plasmodium species

s: Which one of the following zoonotic diseases is transmitted through the bite of a rat flea?
x: Plague is associated with rodents and is transmitted through rat fleas. Rabies is generally transmitted by the bite of infected animals, Nipah is associated with fruit bats and anthrax with infected livestock.
tq: Match the disease with its animal source and transmission route.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kyasanur Forest Disease — rodents through rat fleas
x: Kyasanur Forest Disease is associated with monkeys and is transmitted through ticks. Rodents and rat fleas are associated with plague.
tq: Use the animal-source trap by separating tick-borne and flea-borne diseases.

s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of its usual classification as a zoonotic disease?
x: Rabies, anthrax and Nipah are zoonotic diseases associated with animal sources. Malaria is vector-borne but is not classified as zoonotic in the routine sense used here.
tq: Separate zoonotic diseases from a vector-borne disease that is not routinely classified as zoonotic.

s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding zoonotic and vector-borne diseases?
o: Malaria is both zoonotic and vector-borne in routine classification.
All vector-borne diseases originate in domestic animals.
All zoonotic diseases are transmitted by vectors.
Rabies is zoonotic but not vector-borne in the routine classification.
x: Rabies is a zoonotic disease transmitted mainly through animal bites, but it is not classified as vector-borne. Malaria is vector-borne but not zoonotic in routine classification.
tq: Test the distinction between the overlapping but non-identical categories.

s: Which animal source is associated with anthrax in the zoonotic disease context?
x: Anthrax is associated with infected livestock. Fruit bats are linked with Nipah, birds or poultry with H5N1, and monkeys with Kyasanur Forest Disease.
tq: Use direct animal-source recall with nearby zoonotic distractors.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic and pandemic risk.
2. Mpox is associated with rodents and primates.
3. Rabies is associated with dogs, bats and other wild animals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic risk, Mpox is associated with rodents and primates, and rabies may be transmitted by dogs, bats and other wild animals.
tq: Combine an ecological consequence with two animal-source facts.

s: According to APSES data for 2023, which combination correctly represents malaria and dengue cases in Andhra Pradesh?
x: In 2023, Andhra Pradesh recorded 5,268 malaria cases and 6,453 dengue cases according to the cited APSES data.
tq: Distinguish year-wise paired figures instead of recalling an isolated number.

s: Which of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh’s 2024 malaria and dengue figures?
x: The 2024 figures were 7,871 malaria cases and 5,555 dengue cases, with zero malaria deaths reported in the cited APSES data.
tq: Use the year-number association and reject figures belonging to adjacent years.

s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh in 2025, which of the following is correct?
o: Malaria: 5,268 cases and no deaths; dengue: 6,453 cases and 2 deaths
Malaria: 7,119 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 2,686 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,895 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 1,475 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,871 cases and no deaths; dengue: 5,555 cases and 5 deaths
x: In 2025, Andhra Pradesh recorded 7,119 malaria cases with 8 deaths and 2,686 dengue cases with 5 deaths in the cited data.
tq: Read the paired case-and-death figures together rather than matching cases alone.

s: As reported up to 30 August 2026, which combination is correct for Andhra Pradesh?
x: Up to 30 August 2026, Andhra Pradesh recorded 7,895 malaria cases and 1,475 dengue cases. The reported increases were 27.9% for malaria and 4.6% for dengue.
tq: Anchor the figures to the stated cut-off date before comparing year-wise data.

s: The 2026 rise in malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh was particularly concentrated in which districts or area?
x: The rise in malaria in 2026 was concentrated in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Polavaram and Vizianagaram districts.
tq: Use location-based elimination and avoid substituting other district groups.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported 2026 burden of scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh and its concentration?
o: 1,475 cases, rising in all coastal districts
941 cases, rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam
52 cases, rising in ASR and Kurnool
146 cases, rising in Polavaram and Vizianagaram
x: Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
tq: Match the disease burden figure with the correct geographical concentration.

s: Which statement correctly describes the 2025 Andhra Pradesh figures for AES/JE and chikungunya?
o: AES/JE: 2 cases and 146 deaths; chikungunya: 52 deaths
AES/JE: 146 cases and 8 deaths; chikungunya: 941 cases
AES/JE: 52 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 146 cases
AES/JE: 146 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 52 cases
x: The reported 2025 figures were 146 AES/JE cases with 2 deaths and 52 chikungunya cases.
tq: Keep case and death figures separate while matching the two diseases.

s: Which of the following measures is most directly associated with the response to vector-borne disease burden in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Indoor residual spraying, LLIN mosquito nets and source reduction
Removal of all livestock from tribal districts
Replacement of mosquito control with vaccination alone
Exclusive use of antibiotics and suspension of surveillance
x: The response includes indoor residual spraying, long-lasting insecticidal nets and source reduction. These measures target mosquito vectors and their breeding sites.
tq: Apply the control method to the vector-borne disease scenario.

s: In January 2026, what institutional measure was reported for communicable disease control in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A 12-member national committee on air pollution
A 24-member State task force on communicable diseases
A district-level committee exclusively for dengue vaccines
A 50-member international task force on malaria
x: A 24-member State task force on communicable diseases was constituted in January 2026. High-level committees were also associated with scrub typhus response.
tq: Identify the exact body and membership figure instead of a similar administrative arrangement.

s: Free long-lasting insecticidal nets were reported to cover approximately how many people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, at a cost of Rs 19.25 crore?
x: Free LLINs were reported for approximately 7.80 lakh people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, involving an expenditure of Rs 19.25 crore.
tq: Separate the beneficiary count from the expenditure figure.

s: Which of the following best describes India’s epidemiological transition as reflected in the reported health indicators?
o: Life expectancy increased, but non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths while communicable diseases persist.
Life expectancy remained unchanged and non-communicable diseases account for less than 10% of deaths.
Communicable diseases have disappeared because life expectancy increased.
Life expectancy declined while communicable diseases became the only major cause of death.
x: Life expectancy increased from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023, yet non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths and communicable diseases continue to persist, creating a double burden.
tq: Recognise the double burden by comparing improvements with continuing disease persistence.

s:
Arrange the following reported life-expectancy figures in chronological order:
A. Life expectancy of 70.3 years
B. Life expectancy of 49.7 years
C. Year 2023
D. Year 1973
x: The correct chronological pairing is 49.7 years in 1973 followed by 70.3 years in 2023, represented by B, D, A, C.
tq: Pair each figure with its year before arranging the sequence.

s: Which statement about the geographical distribution of malaria and scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The burden is confined to districts with no tribal population.
The agency districts carry most of the State’s malaria and scrub typhus burden.
Agency districts have no significant vector-borne disease burden.
The burden is concentrated exclusively in the major coastal cities.
x: The agency or tribal districts carry most of Andhra Pradesh’s malaria and scrub typhus burden, making them a priority for surveillance and control.
tq: Use the AP-specific geographical trend and reject absolute location claims.

s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between climate change and vector-borne diseases?
o: Warming generally contracts the range of dengue and malaria vectors.
Vector-borne diseases are unrelated to temperature and extreme weather.
Warming can expand the range of dengue and malaria vectors into new areas.
Climate change affects only water-borne diseases and not vectors.
x: Warming can expand the geographical range of dengue and malaria vectors. Climate change also influences heatwaves, floods and other conditions affecting disease transmission.
tq: Apply the direction of the climate effect rather than choosing the reversed trend.
